#' @keywords internal
bs_sass <- function(theme, ...) {
  # Compilation order:
  #   1. User/brand defaults ($body-color, $primary, etc.)
  #   2. Bootstrap _functions.scss
  #   3. Bootstrap _variables.scss  <- consumes $body-color !default
  #   4. Bootstrap _maps.scss
  #   5. Bootstrap _mixins.scss
  #   6. Bootstrap _root.scss       <- generates --bs-body-color
  #   7. Bootstrap _reboot.scss     <- applies color: var(--bs-body-color) to <body>
  #   8. Bootstrap component .scss files  <- each sets own color
  #   9. bslib component overrides
  #
  # IMPORTANT: Steps 1-2 are where the brand foreground enters.
  # By step 8, the value has been baked into $body-color but
  # component-level colors ($card-color, $nav-link-color, etc.)
  # are derived from DIFFERENT variables, not $body-color.
  
  sass_options <- sass::sass_options(
    output_style = "compressed",
    source_map_embed = FALSE
  )

SUBMIT(answer = "The brand.yml `foreground` color is processed through bslib's Sass pipeline with the following path and a documented gap:

## Path: brand.yml foreground -> CSS

**1. Brand ingestion** (`R/bs-theme-brand.R:47-52`): `bs_theme_brand()` reads `brand$color$foreground` and maps it to `$body-color`.

**2. Sass injection** (`R/bs-theme-update.R`): The value is prepended as `$body-color: <value> !default;` to the Sass bundle, before Bootstrap's own `_variables.scss`.

**3. Sass compilation** (`R/bs-sass.R`): The 9-step pipeline processes the value:
  - Step 3: `_variables.scss` consumes `$body-color`, overriding the default `$gray-900`
  - Step 3 also: ~8 other variables derive from `$body-color` ($body-secondary-color, $text-muted, $dropdown-color, $input-color, $list-group-color, $popover-body-color, $accordion-button-color, $body-tertiary-color)
  - Step 6: `_root.scss` generates `--bs-body-color: <value>` CSS custom property
  - Step 7: `_reboot.scss` applies `color: var(--bs-body-color)` to `<body>`
  - Step 8-9: Component SCSS files use their OWN color variables

## The Gap (bslib #1123)

The foreground color is **partially lost** because of how Bootstrap's Sass architecture separates component colors from body color:

**Components that DO receive foreground:**
- `<body>` text, dropdowns, inputs, list groups, popovers, accordions, tables (via fallback)
- All elements that inherit from `<body>` without intervening color resets

**Components that DON'T receive foreground:**
- Cards (`$card-color: null` - inherits via CSS, breaks in nested contexts)
- Nav links (`$nav-link-color: var(--bs-link-color)` - uses link color)
- Modals (`$modal-content-color: null` - inherits, fragile)
- Navbars (`$navbar-light-color: rgba($black, .55)` - hardcoded)
- bslib value boxes (uses `--bslib-color-fg` custom property)
- Offcanvas (`$offcanvas-color: null` - inherits)

Only 3 CSS selectors in the compiled output reference `var(--bs-body-color)`: body, tables (deep fallback), and select typography elements.

**Shiny secondary gap:** Shiny delegates entirely to bslib, but additionally has hardcoded `color: #333` in `shiny.css` for some widgets.

**Planned fix** (TODO in `R/bs-theme-update.R:42-43`): Map `$body-color` to component-level variables (`$card-color`, `$modal-content-color`, etc.) when brand.yml is active, ensuring the foreground color propagates to all text contexts.")

The brand.yml `foreground` color is processed through bslib's Sass pipeline with the following path and a documented gap:

## Path: brand.yml foreground -> CSS

**1. Brand ingestion** (`R/bs-theme-brand.R:47-52`): `bs_theme_brand()` reads `brand$color$foreground` and maps it to `$body-color`.

**2. Sass injection** (`R/bs-theme-update.R`): The value is prepended as `$body-color: <value> !default;` to the Sass bundle, before Bootstrap's own `_variables.scss`.

**3. Sass compilation** (`R/bs-sass.R`): The 9-step pipeline processes the value:
  - Step 3: `_variables.scss` consumes `$body-color`, overriding the default `$gray-900`
  - Step 3 also: ~8 other variables derive from `$body-color` ($body-secondary-color, $text-muted, $dropdown-color, $input-color, $list-group-color, $popover-body-color, $accordion-button-color, $body-tertiary-color)
  - Step 6: `_root.scss` generates `--bs-body-color: <value>` CSS custom property
  - Step 7: `_reboot.scss` applies `color: var(--bs-body-color)` to `<body>`
  - Step 8-9: Component SCSS files use their OWN color variables

## The Gap (bslib #1123)

The foreground color is **partially lost** because of how Bootstrap's Sass architecture separates component colors from body color:

**Components that DO receive foreground:**
- `<body>` text, dropdowns, inputs, list groups, popovers, accordions, tables (via fallback)
- All elements that inherit from `<body>` without intervening color resets

**Components that DON'T receive foreground:**
- Cards (`$card-color: null` - inherits via CSS, breaks in nested contexts)
- Nav links (`$nav-link-color: var(--bs-link-color)` - uses link color)
- Modals (`$modal-content-color: null` - inherits, fragile)
- Navbars (`$navbar-light-color: rgba($black, .55)` - hardcoded)
- bslib value boxes (uses `--bslib-color-fg` custom property)
- Offcanvas (`$offcanvas-color: null` - inherits)

Only 3 CSS selectors in the compiled output reference `var(--bs-body-color)`: body, tables (deep fallback), and select typography elements.

**Shiny secondary gap:** Shiny delegates entirely to bslib, but additionally has hardcoded `color: #333` in `shiny.css` for some widgets.

**Planned fix** (TODO in `R/bs-theme-update.R:42-43`): Map `$body-color` to component-level variables (`$card-color`, `$modal-content-color`, etc.) when brand.yml is active, ensuring the foreground color propagates to all text contexts.
